history.heading: Island civilisations
paragraphs: The Federated States of Micronesia consist of over 600 islands in four states, Yap, Chuuk, Pohnpei and Kosrae, spread across the western Pacific. The islands were settled by Austronesian peoples thousands of years ago.

On Pohnpei, the Saudeleur dynasty built Nan Madol, a complex of artificial islets with basalt stone buildings, from around the 12th century; it is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Yap is famous for its giant stone money (rai), quarried in Palau.

history.heading: Colonial era and independence
paragraphs: Spain claimed the islands, sold them to Germany in 1899, and Japan took control in 1914. After the Second World War, they became part of the US-administered Trust Territory of the Pacific Islands. The Federated States of Micronesia became independent in 1986 under a Compact of Free Association with the United States.

culture.heading: Diverse islands
paragraphs: English is the official language, and each state has its own languages, such as Chuukese, Pohnpeian, Yapese and Kosraean. Most people are Christian. Traditional chiefs and customs remain important, especially in Yap, where traditional dress and dances are maintained. Sakau (kava) is a ceremonial drink on Pohnpei.

politics.heading: Federal republic
paragraphs: Micronesia is a federal republic. The Congress elects the president from among its at-large senators. The four states have considerable autonomy. Under the Compact, renewed in 2023, the US provides funding and defence, and citizens can live and work in the US. Some in Chuuk have sought independence.

economy.heading: Aid and fishing
paragraphs: The economy depends heavily on US aid, fishing licence fees for tuna, subsistence farming and fishing. Tourism is limited by remoteness. Many Micronesians have emigrated to the US. The currency is the US dollar.
